entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Guglielmo Fieschi, elevated to cardinal-deacon by his uncle Pope Innocent IV on May 28, 1244, was a pivotal figure in the Fieschi family's ascent and a key instrument of papal power during the tumultuous mid-13th century. Born into the powerful Genoese Fieschi family, his cardinalate solidified the practice of papal nepotism, allowing Innocent IV to staff the College of Cardinals with trusted kin, thereby strengthening his authority against the formidable Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II and within the Curia itself. His elevation came at a critical juncture when the Papacy was increasingly asserting its temporal and spiritual supremacy across Europe, often through the strategic deployment of family members in high ecclesiastical office.

Following his elevation, Cardinal Fieschi received the diaconate of Sant'Eustachio and quickly assumed significant administrative responsibilities. He served as the Papal Legate to Lombardy and the Marches of Ancona and Fermo, regions central to the ongoing conflict between the Papacy and the Hohenstaufen emperor. In these capacities, he was tasked with rallying support for the papal cause, administering papal territories, and ensuring the collection of revenues essential for the Church's expansive political and military endeavors. His legatine missions were crucial in maintaining papal influence in northern and central Italy, areas often contested by imperial loyalists and local lords.
